title: Bar Charts, Pie Charts and Comparisons
writing_skill_goal: Learn how to describe and compare static data across different categories using comparative and superlative structures.
core_writing_framework: For charts without dates (static data), you cannot use trend language like 'increased'. Instead, you must use comparison language: higher than, lower than, the most, the least, compared to.

weak_vs_improved.weak_version: Apples are 50%. Bananas are 20%. Oranges are 10%. Apples are big.
weak_vs_improved.improved_version: Apples accounted for the largest proportion of sales at 50%, which was more than double the figure for bananas (20%). Meanwhile, oranges represented the smallest share at merely 10%.
weak_vs_improved.explanation: The weak version simply lists data like a robot. The improved version synthesizes the data by explicitly comparing the categories ('largest proportion', 'more than double', 'smallest share').

step_by_step_build.content: Always point out the maximum and minimum figures. Use superlatives: 'the most significant', 'the lowest percentage', 'accounted for the largest share'.
If two bars or pie slices are almost the same size, group them together in one sentence. 'Both category A and category B stood at approximately 15%.'.
To score higher in Grammar and Lexical Resource, describe differences using fractions or multipliers: 'was twice as high as', 'was exactly half of', 'accounted for a third of'.

common_mistakes: Using time-based words ('increased', 'fell') on a chart that only shows one single year. Static charts have no movement.
Failing to make any comparisons at all, and just writing a list of every number.
Repeating 'The percentage of...' at the start of every sentence.
original_ielts_prompt: The pie charts below show the primary reasons people migrated to and from the UK in 2007.
model_micro_answer: Employment was by far the most common reason for immigration, cited by 30% of arrivals. This figure was exactly double the proportion of those who immigrated for formal study (15%).
image_prompt_fallback: A pie chart and a bar chart side-by-side, with comparative words like 'larger than', 'the most', and 'double' hovering over the different sections.

quiz.question: If a bar chart only shows data for the year 2020, which of the following sentences is INCORRECT?

options.A: Car sales were significantly higher than bicycle sales.
options.C: Cars accounted for the largest proportion of sales.
options.D: The figure for bicycles was half that of cars.

quiz.explanation: Because the chart only shows one year, there is no passage of time. Therefore, nothing can 'increase' or 'decrease'. You must use comparative language, not trend language.
